topic.angle: Price settles where wants meet supply

card.title: Supply and demand is an old idea

body.claim: A fourteenth-century scholar wrote that if desire for a good rises while its availability falls, its price rises.
body.why: Ibn Taymiyyah added that if availability rises and desire falls, the price comes down. In a perfectly competitive market, the price varies until it settles at the market-clearing price, where the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied.

probes.question: At the market-clearing price, which two quantities are equal?
True or false: if desire for a good rises while its availability falls, its price tends to fall.

claims.claim: A fourteenth-century scholar (Ibn Taymiyyah) wrote that if desire rises while availability falls, price rises
claims.quote: If desire for goods increases while its availability decreases, its price rises.
claims.note: Page: fourteenth-century Syrian scholar Ibn Taymiyyah wrote this.

claims.claim: Ibn Taymiyyah was a fourteenth-century scholar
claims.quote: the power of supply and demand was understood to some extent by several early Muslim scholars, such as fourteenth-century Syrian scholar Ibn Taymiyyah

claims.claim: Ibn Taymiyyah added that if availability rises and desire falls, the price comes down
claims.quote: On the other hand, if availability of the good increases and the desire for it decreases, the price comes down.

claims.claim: In a perfectly competitive market the price varies until it settles at the market-clearing price
claims.quote: will vary until it settles at the market-clearing price

claims.claim: At the market-clearing price quantity demanded equals quantity supplied (probe p1)
claims.quote: where the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied such that an economic equilibrium is achieved

claims.claim: Probe p2 (false): if desire rises while availability falls, price tends to fall - contradicted, price rises
claims.quote: If desire for goods increases while its availability decreases, its price rises.
